The score function is the vector of the two partial derivatives:

$$
\score(\mean, \varpar) =
\begin{pmatrix}
\deriv{\mean}\ell(\mean, \varpar) \\
\deriv{\varpar}\ell(\mean, \varpar)
\end{pmatrix}
$$

For the first entry,
only the last term of $\ell$ depends on $\mean$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mean}\ell
&= \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}
 - \frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(Gaussian log-likelihood)}\\
&= \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi}} + \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
 + \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 + 0 + \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}\\
&= \deriv{\mean}\paren{-\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero terms)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\deriv{\mean}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin \deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin 2(x_i - \mean)\deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(chain rule, outer function $u^2$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The inner derivative is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mean}(x_i - \mean)
&= \deriv{\mean} x_i - \deriv{\mean} \mean
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 - \deriv{\mean} \mean
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\mean$)}\\
&= 0 - 1
&& \text{(derivative of $\mean$ with respect to itself)}\\
&= -1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the inner derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\mean}\ell
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin 2(x_i - \mean) \cdot (-1)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar}\sumin -2(x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\varpar} \cdot (-2) \sumin (x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(factor the constant $-2$ out of the sum)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\sumin (x_i - \mean)
&& \text{(multiply the constants)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - \sumin \mean}
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\varpar}\paren{\sumin x_i - n\mean}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\mean$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

For the second entry,
write $\varpar$ as a single variable $v$, so that $\ell$ contains
$-\frac{n}{2}\log v$ and $-\frac{1}{2}v^{-1}\sum_i (x_i - \mean)^2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\varpar}\ell
&= \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}
 - \frac{1}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(Gaussian log-likelihood)}\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi}} + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
 + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}\\
&= 0 + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
 + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
 + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}\\
&= \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\varpar}}
 + \deriv{\varpar}\paren{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \paren{\varpar}^{-1}}
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\deriv{\varpar}\logf{\varpar}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \deriv{\varpar}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \deriv{\varpar}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of $\log v$)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
 - \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \paren{-\paren{\varpar}^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule for $v^{-1}$)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
 + \frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2 \paren{\varpar}^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-1}
 + \frac{1}{2}\paren{\varpar}^{-2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\end{aligned}
$$
